user_input: Everyone in my wing already has their 'group' for the project labs and dinner. I sat in the mess hall for 45 minutes today pretending to scroll through LinkedIn updates just so I wouldn't look like a total loser eating alone. It's only the first semester of BTech and I already feel like an absolute ghost here.

My roommate got placed at a tier-1 firm today and his phone has been buzzing with congrats messages non-stop. Meanwhile, I'm sitting on my bunk bed staring at my DSA lab backlogs, with zero unread chats on my WhatsApp. My dad called to ask if I've secured a package yet, and I just hung up because the silence in this room is literally suffocating me.

It's the long weekend and literally every single person in my corridor went back home or on a trip to the hills. I couldn't go because of my internal test retakes, and now the hostel wing is so quiet I can hear the ceiling fan buzzing. I tried coding to distract myself, but I ended up crying over a basic array sorting problem because I realized nobody would even notice if I just disappeared from this campus.

The professor told us to partner up for the OS design lab and my heart literally stopped. I stood there near the whiteboard for ten minutes waiting for someone to look at me, but everyone was already high-fiving and forming teams of four. I had to go up to the teacher's desk and ask to be manually assigned to a random group—the pity looks they gave me made me want to jump out of the window.

Today is my 20th birthday and my phone only got automated HBD emails from the college library and my bank. I've been scrolling through Instagram stories of people in my batch posting surprise midnight cake-smash videos for their friends. I'm sitting here in the dark eating cold Maggi, wondering what is so fundamentally broken in me that I couldn't make even one real friend in two years of college.

It's Friday night and my entire wing is empty. Everyone went out to celebrate after the DSA midterms, and I'm just sitting here in my room staring at the ceiling. I messed up my trees and graphs questions, and honestly, seeing their Whatsapp status updates of them drinking and laughing at some pub down the road makes me want to throw up. I’ve been here for six months and I still don't have a single person I can text to just grab a chai. I feel completely invisible, like if I didn't show up to the lab tomorrow, literally no one would notice.

They announced the capstone project groups today and my heart literally dropped to my stomach. The professor said 'form teams of four,' and within two seconds, everyone was turning around, laughing, and high-fiving. I just sat there pretending to debug my SQL code so I wouldn't look like a total loser while everyone else paired up. Eventually, the TA had to randomly assign me to a group that already had three friends who clearly didn't want a random stranger ruining their CGPA. I hate this place so much, I feel like a parasite.

My roommate's parents keep calling him, and he’s always talking about his plans with his friends from the coding club, telling his mom how he got a referral. Meanwhile, my mom called today asking why I haven't posted any photos from college events or if I've made 'good friends' yet. I lied and said I was too busy with my operating systems backlog. The truth is, I spend my weekends sleeping 14 hours just to make the days go by faster so I don't have to walk down the corridor and see everyone hanging out in groups. I’m so exhausted from pretending I’m okay.

I went to the hostel mess tonight and it was absolutely packed because of the festive special dinner. I walked in with my plate, looked around at all the crowded tables of people laughing and sharing food, and I just couldn't do it. My chest felt so tight I could barely breathe, so I turned right back around and walked to my room to eat some dry Maggi instead. I feel like such a coward. Why is making friends so easy for literally everyone else, while I can't even sit in a dining hall without having a panic attack?

It's my 20th birthday today. Not a single person on campus has messaged me or knocked on my door to wish me. The only texts I got were from my service provider and a generic email from the university library. I see people getting their faces covered in cake in the hostel courtyard at midnight all the time, but for me, it's just another Tuesday night staring at my compiler design notes. I've spent two years here and realized that if I disappeared tomorrow, my hostel room would just be cleared out for the next roll number without a single tear shed.

It's Friday night and my entire hostel wing has gone out to some cafe or club, I don't even know. I'm just sitting here in my dark room, staring at my pending DSA coding lab assignment and listening to the echoes of people laughing in the corridor. I haven't spoken to a single human being today except for saying 'one plate idli' to the mess uncle this morning. I feel so invisible, like if I just packed my bags and left this college tomorrow, absolutely nobody would notice or care.

The professor announced a group project for our Web Dev lab today and said 'find your own partners.' Within five seconds, everyone was turning around, high-fiving, and making groups. I just sat there staring at my laptop screen, pretending to debug a line of code so I wouldn't look like a total loser who has zero friends. Now I have to email the TA to manually assign me to some random group that probably doesn't want me anyway. I hate this place so much, the embarrassment is literally eating me alive.

I scrolled past five different Instagram stories of my batchmates posing at some birthday party in Pune, and it hit me that I wasn't even considered for an invite. Back home, I had a group, I was someone who people actually liked talking to. Here, my CGPA is tanking, I failed my midterms, and my parents keep calling me to ask why I haven't got a placement offer yet like Sharmaji's son. I feel like such a failure on every level, totally disconnected from who I used to be.

I dread going to the mess hall for dinner. Walking in with a steel tray, looking around a room of two hundred people screaming and laughing at their tables, and trying to find a single empty spot where I won't feel like an awkward intruder is exhausting. I usually just swallow my food as fast as possible in five minutes while staring at my phone, pretending to read a tech newsletter, and then run back to my hostel room. I'm so tired of pretending I'm too busy to make friends when the truth is I'm just utterly terrified of rejection.

My roommate got placed today at a top-tier tech firm, and his phone has been ringing non-stop with congratulations. His friends literally broke into our room to dump cake on him and drag him out to celebrate, while I just sat on my bed pretending to study for my backlogs. I had to force this fake, plastic smile on my face to congratulate him when inside, my chest felt so tight I could barely breathe. I am genuinely happy for him, but the stark contrast of his success and my absolute isolation makes me feel like a ghost haunting my own room.

It's been three months since college started, and every single evening is a nightmare. I literally dread the dinner bell because I know I have to walk into the mess hall and look for an empty corner table, or worse, ask a group 'is this seat taken' only to get those half-hearted 'uh, yeah' nods. Today, while everyone was making plans for the weekend trip in the hostel WhatsApp group, I just stared at my phone screen in my dark room. I'm struggling with my DSA labs, my midterms were a disaster, and I have absolutely no one to talk to or cry with. I feel like a complete ghost walking through these corridors.

Everyone in my wing is celebrating. Sharmaji's son got a 14 LPA package, my roommate got placed in a product-based company today, and my parents keep calling me asking why my name isn't on the placement coordinator's PDF list yet. I haven't even cleared the first round of coding tests, and honestly, the worst part isn't the rejection—it's that I have no friends to even vent to. I just lock my door and pretend to sleep so I don't have to hear them ordering pizza and cheering next door. I feel so utterly left behind, like I'm a defective piece in a factory of successful machines.

We had to form groups of four for the DBMS mini-project today in the lab. The professor said 'find your own partners' and my heart just dropped into my stomach. I stood there pretending to adjust my laptop bag while everyone scrambled to team up with their friends, and eventually, the lab assistant had to awkwardly force me into a group that already had three people who clearly didn't want a stranger. They didn't even add me to their Google Meet, they just assigned me a minor documentation part over WhatsApp without asking. I’m paying so much fees here, but I feel like an unwanted charity case who doesn't exist to anyone unless they need a filler.

It's the long Diwali weekend and almost the entire hostel has gone home. I couldn't go because I have three backlogs to clear and need to prepare for the re-exams next week. The silence in this corridor is literally choking me; even the mess is running on a limited menu and there's nobody in the common room. I scrolled through Instagram for four hours today seeing everyone's family photos and card parties with their high school friends, and I just burst out crying. I have no friends here, no home to go back to where I feel wanted, and my mind keeps telling me I'll always be this alone.

I moved from the North to this college in the South, and I don't speak the regional language. Every time I sit in the canteen, everyone around me switches to their mother tongue, laughing and sharing inside jokes. I try to smile and nod along, but I can feel this thick, invisible wall between us. Yesterday was my birthday, and the only notification I got was from the college library system reminding me of an overdue book. I feel so incredibly stupid for thinking I could make a life here; I'm just a misfit who doesn't belong anywhere.

It’s been three months at this hostel and I still dread the 8 PM dinner walk. Everyone walks to the mess in these loud, laughing groups of four or five, and I’m always just lagging behind, pretending to check my phone so I don't look like a total loser. Today we had to form pairs for the DSA lab projects and the professor just looked at me and said 'anyone else left?' in front of the whole class of 120 people while I just stared at my desk. I'm paying lakhs in fees, pulling 18-hour study sessions, but at night I just stare at the ceiling feeling completely invisible.

My dad called today to ask if I got short-listed for the FinTech internships, and when I told him no, he started listing out my cousin's package and how he already has a core circle of 'networking buddies' in his college. I hung up and opened my WhatsApp, but the only unread messages were from my college service provider and the official batch announcement group. Everyone else is out celebrating their midterms at some café down the street, and I’m sitting in my 8x8 hostel room staring at a DSA tree traversal code that won't compile, wondering why I'm so bad at both coding and making people like me.

Today is my 20th birthday and not a single person in this wing came to my room to do the usual midnight cake-smashing thing they do for everyone else. I saw the WhatsApp stories of the guy next door getting dragged out of his room at 12 AM with 30 people cheering, while I sat here eating a cold packet of Maggi alone in the dark. It’s funny because I actually tried talking to people during the induction week, but I guess I’m just that forgettable background character who doesn't matter to anyone here.

Everyone in my wing speaks Telugu or Hindi fluently and they all huddle in the corridor at midnight laughing at jokes I don't get, sharing home-cooked food their moms sent. I stand by my door wanting to join, but my throat just tightens up and I end up locking my door and putting my headphones on to drown out their laughter. I've started skipping the common room entirely because the silence of my own thoughts is somehow less painful than standing in a group of ten people and feeling completely invisible.

It’s Sunday evening and I haven't spoken a single word out loud since Friday afternoon when I said 'thank you' to the delivery guy. I had a fever all weekend and literally lay in my bunk bed shivering, while my roommates went on a road trip to Lonavala and posted thirty photos on Instagram with the hashtag 'squadgoals'. No one even texted to check if I was still alive or if I needed paracetamol from the campus clinic. I feel like if I packed my bags and left this college tomorrow, my room would just be empty and no one would even notice I was gone.

It’s 9 PM on a Friday and the hostel corridor is so loud with guys planning their weekend trips, but I'm just sitting here staring at my DSA coding assignment that won't compile. I tried going down to the mess for dinner earlier, but every single table was packed with groups laughing, so I just bought a packet of chips from the canteen and came back. I’ve been in this college for five months now and I still don't have a single person I can ping to grab tea with. I feel like a complete ghost, like if I didn't show up to the lab tomorrow, literally no one would even notice my seat is empty.

We had to form groups of four for our web dev capstone project today, and it was the most humiliating ten minutes of my semester. The professor said 'find your teammates' and immediately everyone started turning around, making eye contact, and laughing while I just sat there staring at my laptop screen, pretending to edit my GitHub profile. Eventually, I was the last one left and the professor had to forcefully assign me to a group that clearly didn't want me because they already had their 'squad'. I’ve got a decent CGPA but socially I'm a complete failure, and I dread every single class now.

My dad called me today to ask why I haven't posted any photos with college friends on the family group, and then he started comparing me to my cousin who got a 20 LPA package and has a massive friend circle. I couldn't even tell him that I spent my entire weekend inside my hostel room eating instant noodles and studying OS backlogs just to avoid seeing people. Everyone else is sharing LinkedIn updates about their dream internships while I don't even have a single person to share my anxiety with. I feel so incredibly small and unlovable when the only notifications on my phone are from system updates and OTPs.

I deleted Instagram today because I couldn't take it anymore. Every Friday night it's the same thing—scrolling through stories of classmates from my batch heading out to cafes, celebrating birthdays in the hostel corridors at midnight, and going on trips to the hills. I'm in my second year of engineering and my contact list is basically just my mom, my dad, and a couple of delivery drivers. I feel like there's some secret handbook on 'how to make friends' that everyone else received at orientation, and I somehow missed the distribution.

Since I came to this college from another state, I feel completely locked out of the social circles here because everyone immediately clusters into their own regional language groups during breaks. In the hostel mess, they all sit together speaking their native tongue and laughing at inside jokes, while I just nod politely and eat my cold roti in silence. I tried joining the debate club hoping to meet people, but even there, the senior cliques are so tight that newbies are basically treated like furniture. I'm starting to think I’m just fundamentally incompatible with this place and that I'll spend the next three years entirely alone.

I’m in my third semester now and my GPA is slipping because I can’t even get myself to go to the DSA lab anymore. What’s the point? Everyone already has their tight little friend circles. During the midterms, they all studied together in the library, and I was just sitting in my hostel room, staring at my wall. When we have to form groups of three for the web-dev project next week, I know I'll be the leftover one the professor just dumps into some random group where they'll ignore me. I feel like an absolute ghost walking through these corridors.

Friday nights are the absolute worst. I hear the guys next door laughing, playing FIFA, and talking about which club they're heading to. I’m just lying on my bunk bed in the dark, refreshing LinkedIn and Instagram, watching everyone post pictures of their weekend getaways or placement offer celebrations. My dad called today and asked if I made friends to study with, and I had to lie and say yeah, otherwise he'd start comparing me to my cousin who already has a 12 LPA job offer and a huge group. I'm so tired of pretending I exist here.

I hate the mess hall. I literally skip dinner half the time and just eat Maggi in my room because walking into that noisy hall and seeing zero empty seats next to anyone I know is humiliating. Last week I sat at an empty table, and a group came, looked at me, and chose a different table across the room. I feel so ugly and unlikable, like there's some invisible warning sign on my forehead that tells people to stay away from me.

It's my birthday tomorrow. Nobody in this college knows, and honestly, nobody would care even if they did. Back home, my high school friends and I used to do late-night cake cuttings, but here, I'll probably just spend the night debugging my backlog OS lab codes alone. I saw a group down the corridor putting up fairy lights and singing for some guy at midnight yesterday, and it physically ached in my chest. I’ve been here for a year and I haven't made a single deep connection. I think I'm just broken.

I tried joining the coding club and the literary society to meet people, but it’s like everyone else already arrived with pre-made friend groups from their coaching institutes. I stand at the edge of the circles, pretending to look at my phone, hoping someone will just say hello, but I’m completely invisible. Eventually, I just quietly slip away and walk back to my room in the dark. I have zero energy left to keep putting myself out there just to be rejected over and over again.

It’s been four months in this hostel and I still sit alone during dinner. Tonight I saw the guys from my DSA lab laughing at some inside joke, and I just stared at my plate of cold rotis, feeling like an absolute ghost. My roommate has already found his 'squad' and they're out celebrating some placement offer, while I'm just here staring at my backlog syllabus wondering what's wrong with me.

We had to form groups of four for the final year capstone project today. The professor said 'find your partners' and within thirty seconds, the entire lab shuffled into their neat little cliques, leaving me standing there like an idiot until the TA manually assigned me to a random group that didn't even want me. My dad called later asking if I got into a good project team to secure a high package, and I just lied because I couldn't bear to tell him I have zero friends here.

It's Saturday night, the hostel corridor is dead silent because everyone went out to some pub or café, and I'm just lying on my bed staring at the ceiling. I opened Instagram and saw stories of my batchmates clinking glasses, and my chest physically ached with this weird panic that I'm going to spend my entire youth completely alone. My CGPA is slipping, I don't have a single person to text, and I feel like I'm slowly rotting in this single-seater room.

The placement drive results came out today and my WhatsApp is flooded with 'Congratulate XYZ' messages in the official batch group. Everyone is celebrating, planning trips, and making plans to move to Bangalore or Gurgaon together, but I didn't clear the coding round and have nobody to even talk to about how scary this is. I feel this horrible, bitter jealousy toward them for having both the high-paying jobs and the perfect friendship circles while I have absolutely nothing.

I hear the guys in the room next to me laughing and talking late into the night, sharing their relationship dramas and complaining about the system admin professor. I'm sitting here with my headphones pressed tightly against my ears, trying to block out their voices because the sheer warmth of their friendship makes my chest feel empty. I used to be the funny guy in my high school back home, but here in this competitive pressure cooker, I’ve forgotten how to talk to people, and I feel like that version of me is dead.

It's always the same thing during the Tuesday DSA lab. The professor says, 'Find a partner for the semester project,' and everyone instantly looks at each other, pairing up in seconds. I've been in this college for two semesters now and I don't have a single person I can text to ask about the assignment. I feel like an absolute ghost walking through these hallways.

I literally dread dinner time. Yesterday, I sat at a table with three guys from my wing and they just talked in their regional language, laughing at inside jokes while I stared down at my cold rotis. I am so tired of eating every single meal in complete silence, pretending to watch coding videos on my phone so I look busy.

I opened Instagram and saw everyone's stories at the cafe down the road, and my chest literally hurts. Is there something fundamentally wrong with me that makes me so unlikable?

Everyone is posting their placement updates on LinkedIn, 'thrilled to share' this, 'excited to join' that. I didn't get shortlisted for the second round of any company this week, and honestly, the academic failure hurts, but the social part is killing me. My dad called and asked why my classmate got a 12 LPA package while I'm still struggling with backlogs. I have no one here to talk to about how terrified I am. If I fail these placements, I'll be leaving college without a job and without a single friend.

Today was my 20th birthday. Back home, my parents called and sang to me, which just made me want to cry. Here at college, not a single person noticed or said anything. I sat in the library until 10 PM doing my operating systems assignment, hoping maybe my roommate would have a small pastry or something when I got back. He was just asleep with his headphones on. I'm sitting on the fire escape right now looking at the city lights, wondering if my absence would even register to anyone in this entire city.

I feel like a ghost walking through these corridors, just watching everyone else live their best college lives while my phone has zero notifications. Am I just fundamentally unlikable or what?

I feel so invisible in this hostel, like if I disappeared tonight, it would take them days to notice my empty bed.

It's Saturday night and the entire hostel wing is empty because everyone went on a road trip to the hills, and I wasn't even on the WhatsApp group where they planned it. I'm just sitting here listening to my roommate's mechanical keyboard click in the silence, scrolling through their Instagram stories of bonfires and inside jokes. I've tried joining clubs, I tried talking to people during orientation, but I'm just that weird guy who sits in the back and gets forgotten when the plans actually happen.

Being at this university is so exhausting because everyone immediately sorted themselves into regional language groups and cliques, and since I don't fit into any of them, I'm just stranded. During the project group formation today, I literally stood there frozen while everyone spoke in their mother tongues, and I had to walk up to the professor like a child begging to be placed somewhere. I feel like there's some secret code to making friends that everyone else received at birth, and I somehow missed the memo.

Today is my 21st birthday and the only notifications on my phone are automated emails from my bank and a text from my mom. I watched the guys next door get cake-smashed on their faces last night, screaming and laughing, and it just made my chest ache so bad I couldn't breathe. I've spent three years here grinding for my GPA, but what's the point of a good package if I have to celebrate every single milestone completely alone in a dark room?

I've been in college for three months now, and I still sit alone in the mess during dinner. Every single evening, I watch these tight-knit squads laughing, sharing food, and planning their weekend trips, while I just stare down at my plate, pretending I'm super focused on a DSA coding video on my phone so I don't look like a total freak. I tried talking to a guy in my lab last week, but it was just awkward small talk and then he ran off to join his actual friends. I feel like an absolute ghost walking through these corridors, and I honestly don't know how much longer I can keep pretending I'm okay with being completely invisible.

It is another Friday night and my hostel room is basically a tomb. I can hear the guys next door shouting and playing FIFA, and my phone hasn't buzzed with a personal text in three days unless you count the automated placement cell notifications on WhatsApp. I have two backlogs from last semester, my CGPA is a joke, and my parents keep sending me screenshots of my cousin's high-package placement offer at some MNC. I feel like such a massive disappointment to everyone, and because I have zero friends here to even vent to, I just lie on this hard cot staring at the ceiling fan until 3 AM, feeling entirely hollow inside.

We had to form groups of four for our final year software engineering project today, and the lab coordinator literally had to assign me to a random group because nobody chose me. Everyone else in my hostel wing speaks a different regional language, and they all formed their groups within five minutes of the class starting. I just stood there at the podium like an idiot while the professor asked who wanted to take me in, and everyone just looked at their laptops. I've never felt so rejected and humiliated in my entire life; it's like my lack of social skills is a disease that everyone else can see, and I'm forced to carry it alone.

It's raining heavily outside and I'm just scrolling through my high school group chat on WhatsApp. None of them have replied to my memes in weeks, and I can see from their Instagram stories that they've all made new, cooler friend groups at their respective universities. I'm sitting here with a cold cup of tea, failing my midterms, with absolutely no one to talk to or even walk to the local tea stall with. I feel like my past has completely evaporated and I have absolutely no future here; I'm just a ghost haunting this tiny hostel room while everyone else is moving on with their lives.

The college cultural fest is happening right now outside my window—I can literally hear the bass from the concert shaking my walls. Everyone in the hostel dressed up, took group photos in the corridor, and headed out together, laughing and talking. I pretended I had a terrible migraine and locked my door because the thought of walking around the festival ground alone, watching couples and friend groups take selfies, made me want to throw up. I am sitting here in the dark, eating instant noodles, feeling like a complete failure of a human being who doesn't even know how to make a single friend.

It's been four months in this hostel and I still dread lunch. Today during the DSA lab, the prof said 'form pairs' and literally everyone immediately turned to their friends while I just sat there staring at my terminal pretend-coding. I ended up getting paired with the guy who didn't show up. I eat my mess meals in under five minutes just so I can run back to my room and lock the door.

Every Friday night, the entire wing of my hostel lights up. I hear them laughing, ordering pizza, and planning trips in their regional language groups, and I’m just staring at the ceiling of my room with my noise-canceling headphones on. My dad called today asking if I made friends to study with for midterms, and I lied and said yes. I feel like a total fraud and an outsider in my own college.

Today was my 20th birthday and not a single person on this campus knew or cared. I saw on WhatsApp that the guy who sits next to me in Web Dev had this massive cake-smashing celebration in the hostel corridor with 20 people pouring water on him. I just sat in the dark eating a packet of Lays and trying to debug my React project. If I can't even get people to talk to me, how am I ever going to survive the placement season?

We had to choose mini-project groups today for DBMS. I posted in the class WhatsApp group asking if anyone had space, and my message just got read-receipted by 80 people with no reply. Then I watched two guys who sit behind me form a group in seconds. I feel so utterly disposable here, like if I stopped showing up to classes tomorrow, my seat would just be empty and nobody would even ask the professor where I went.

I got down with high fever last week and missed three days of classes. Nobody texted to ask why I was absent, or if I needed food from the mess. Meanwhile, my roommate got a 12 LPA internship offer and his phone has been ringing non-stop with congratulations. I'm lying here shivering, feeling like an absolute ghost in this massive campus of 5000 people. I'm so tired of trying to fit in.

Everyone in my DSA lab already has their 'group' sorted out. I sat there for two hours today debugging my linked list code entirely alone, and when the lab ended, they all went to the canteen together laughing. I ended up walking back to my hostel room, locked the door, and skipped dinner because the thought of sitting alone in the mess hall while everyone is shouting and sharing food makes me want to throw up. It’s been five months of this; I feel like an absolute ghost on this campus.

It's a Friday night and my phone is completely dry, not a single WhatsApp notification except for the college placement cell updates. My dad called today screaming about how my cousin bagged a 15 LPA package while I'm struggling with a 7.5 CGPA and have zero friends to even talk to or vent. I see people in the corridor ordering pizza and celebrating their shortlists together, and I'm just lying here staring at the fan, wondering what is fundamentally wrong with me that nobody wants to be around me.

The professor announced the major project groups today and said 'find your own teams of four.' My heart literally dropped to my stomach because I knew exactly what would happen. I stood there awkwardly while everyone scrambled to team up with their friends, and I had to go up to the teacher's podium like a loser to ask him to assign me to a random group that clearly didn't want me. I've never felt so deeply unwanted and humiliated in my entire life.

It's the long holiday weekend and the entire hostel wing is a graveyard because everyone went on road trips or back home. I couldn't afford the train ticket home because of my backlogs prep, so I'm just here alone in this damp room. I made the mistake of opening Instagram and seeing stories of my batchmates drinking and clicking photos in cafes, and it just hit me that if I disappeared from this college tomorrow, literally no one would notice or care.

Yesterday was my 20th birthday. I spent the entire day hoping at least my roommate would notice or say something, but he just grabbed his keys and went to a party. At midnight, I heard the room next door screaming and smashing cake on some guy's face, playing music, while I sat on my bed eating a cold samosa I bought from the tuck shop. I ended up crying myself to sleep under my blanket so they wouldn't hear me through the thin hostel walls.

It's Friday night and my entire hostel wing is out. I can hear them laughing down the corridor, probably heading to some cafe, while I'm just sitting here staring at my LeetCode dashboard trying to fix this dumb segmentation fault. I've been in college for a whole semester now, but my WhatsApp has literally zero chats except for the official class group. It's like if I don't initiate, I don't exist to anyone here.

I completely messed up my DSA midterms and when everyone was discussing their scores outside the exam hall, I just slipped away to the washroom. I stayed in the cubicle for twenty minutes just to avoid walking back to the hostel alone because everyone else was in groups. My parents keep asking about my CGPA and packages, but I don't even have a single person to sit with during the lunch mess, let alone talk about my stress.

It was my birthday yesterday. I stayed up till midnight hoping maybe someone from my project group or my lab partner would drop a text, but nothing. Just a dry automated email from the college library about a pending book return. I ended up ordering a single pastry from Swiggy and eating it in the dark while my roommate was out celebrating his placement with his friends.

We had to form groups of four for our web development capstone project today. The professor said 'find your partners' and the whole lab immediately erupted into chatter and desk-shuffling. I just sat there frozen, pretending to debug a working line of code, waiting for the professor to finally assign me to whatever group had a leftover slot because nobody chose me. I feel like an absolute ghost in this department.

Every evening I scroll through Instagram and see stories of people from my branch going on weekend trips or just chilling at local cafes. I've tried joining the debate club and the coding club, but everyone already has their tight-knit circles from freshman year orientation. I'm just the guy who sits on the last bench, takes notes, and walks back to an empty hostel room where my own voice feels foreign to me.

It's 9 PM and I've been staring at my DSA lab assignment for four hours. Everyone in my hostel wing has gone out to the local tea stall together; I heard them laughing and planning it right outside my door, but nobody knocked. I ended up sitting in the mess hall alone for dinner, pretending to scroll through LinkedIn updates just so I wouldn't look like a total loser. My CGPA is slipping, my backlogs are piling up, and I don't have a single person here I can call a friend. I feel like a complete ghost walking through this campus.

We had to form groups of four for our web development capstone project today. The professor stood there counting heads, and of course, I was the leftover one who didn't have a team because everyone else already had their tight-knit circles. He had to awkwardly force me into a group that clearly didn't want me, and the silence when I sat down at their table was deafening. I just stared at my hands, feeling this hot wave of shame because I've been in this college for two semesters and I still have nobody. I'm terrified of graduating without making a single real connection.

It is Friday night in the hostel and the silence in my room is suffocating. I can hear the bass from speakers in the next room where they're celebrating someone's placement offer, but my phone hasn't vibrated in three days except for OTPs and a message from my dad asking if I cleared my coding rounds. I tried to study but the anxiety is making my chest so tight I can barely breathe. It feels like everyone is moving forward, getting jobs, making memories, and I'm just trapped in this dark room, completely forgotten.

Today is my birthday. My parents called me in the morning to wish me, which was nice, but on campus, absolutely nobody knew or cared. I sat through three hours of lectures watching my classmates throw massive cake-smearing surprises for someone else in the corridor, laughing and taking photos for Instagram. I went back to my room, locked the door, and just cried because I realized if I packed my bags and left this place tomorrow, not a single peer would notice my absence. I feel totally invisible.

I moved to this city for college three months ago and the language barrier is completely killing me. In the hostel mess and during labs, everyone immediately groups up based on their home states and starts speaking in their regional languages, laughing at inside jokes I have zero context for. I just stand on the margins, nodding awkwardly, feeling like an alien who doesn't belong anywhere. I tried joining the debate club to meet people but I froze up during the icebreaker and now I just stay in my room, too scared of rejection to even try talking anymore.

Everyone got into their friend groups during orientation week, but I was late to campus because of my compartment exam. Now, during dinner in the hostel mess, I just sit at the absolute edge of the long tables, staring at my plate of cold rotis while the adjacent table bursts into laughter about some wing-inside-joke. My phone has literally zero notifications except for college circulars. I feel like a complete ghost, wandering around campus without anyone realizing I exist.

DSA coding labs are a nightmare because the professor always says 'form groups of two for the project' and everybody immediately locks eyes with their friends in two seconds. I just sit there staring at my VS Code screen, pretending I'm super focused on debugging some random code, waiting for the teacher to awkwardly pair me with whatever leftover student didn't show up or doesn't care. It makes me feel so pathetic, like I'm some defective product nobody wants to partner with.

It's Friday night and my entire wing is dead quiet because everyone went out to some cafe or birthday party in town. I can see their Instagram stories of lit-up cafes, while I'm just lying on my dusty hostel bed with a single LED tube light on, staring at the ceiling fan. I ended up ordering a single roll from the canteen and eating it alone in the dark because I didn't want the security guard at the mess to look at me and pity me. I feel so fundamentally unlovable.

My mom called me today and the first thing she asked was if I've made close friends yet, because my cousin in another college is already going on weekend trips with his group. I panicked and lied, saying I have a big group and we hang out all the time. In reality, the only person who spoke to me today was the librarian when I returned my textbooks. I'm drowning in backlogs, my CGPA is slipping, and I have absolutely no one to sit with and just cry. If I fail, I fail alone.

I tried so hard to be social during the cultural fest. I joined the volunteer team, helped carry heavy speakers, and painted banners until 2 AM thinking maybe this is how I finally make friends. But as soon as the fest ended, they all went out for a celebratory dinner and literally forgot to add me to the taxi group chat. I stood near the campus gate watching them drive off laughing, and realized I'm just a convenient extra set of hands to everyone, never someone they actually want around.
